subject: Live2D Cubism
title: Live2D Cubism Alternatives in 2026
description: Ten Live2D Cubism alternatives for avatar rigging: Inochi2D, VRoid Studio, Blender, Reallusion, Spine, Rive, Moho, Animaze, Warudo and VTube Studio.
intro: Live2D Cubism Editor builds 2D-based three-dimensional expression from a single illustration, and it is the rigging tool behind many VTuber avatars. Operated by 株式会社 Live2D, the editor comes in PRO and FREE versions, with a 42-day PRO trial before the free version continues. Artists who want a fully open framework, a 3D avatar pipeline or a different animation style look elsewhere. The ten options here lean toward free or open tools where they exist, with paid rigging tools and streaming avatar apps added for artists who want a different route.
why_switch: Cubism Editor PRO is sold through the Live2D Store, and the amounts were not on the pages we opened, so artists budget by checking the store directly.
After the 42-day PRO trial, the FREE version continues, which keeps some artists on a reduced feature set they would rather replace with an open tool.
Open-source fans prefer Inochi2D, a framework for real-time 2D puppet animation that says real-time character animation is royalty-free.
Some creators want a 3D avatar instead of a 2D puppet. VRoid Studio and Reallusion are built around 3D characters.
Game animators who need bones and meshes for sprite work, not face expressions, move to Spine or Rive.
Streamers who want to go live quickly sometimes skip rigging and use an avatar app such as Animaze or Warudo.

picks.name: Inochi2D
picks.pricing: No price on the homepage; it has Download and Donate links.
picks.note: Inochi2D describes itself as a framework for real-time 2D puppet animation using 2D meshes and layering, used for VTubing and games development. It says real-time character animation is royalty-free. It is the most direct swap for the free-or-open angle, though you should expect a smaller ecosystem of tutorials and model sellers than Live2D has.

sources.fact: Inochi2D's homepage describes it as a framework for real-time 2D puppet animation using 2D meshes and layering.
Inochi2D's homepage says it is used for VTubing and games development.
Inochi2D's homepage says real-time character animation is royalty-free.

picks.name: VRoid Studio
picks.pricing: No pricing shown on the FAQ hub page opened.
picks.note: VRoid Studio is listed as a 3D character creation tool on the VRoid FAQ hub, alongside VRoid Hub, Mobile, SDK and WEAR. It changes the workflow from rigging a drawing to sculpting a 3D character. The hub is in English and Japanese, which helps when you need to look up how to export for tracking apps.

sources.fact: The VRoid FAQ hub lists VRoid Studio as a 3D character creation tool, version 1.0.0 and later in its stable release.
The VRoid FAQ hub lists VRoid Hub, VRoid Mobile, VRoid SDK and VRoid WEAR as other products in the VRoid family.
The VRoid FAQ hub is published in English and Japanese.

picks.name: Blender
picks.best_for: Free general 3D tool with GPL terms
picks.pricing: No price on the opened manual pages; the manual has a section on free software and the GPL.
picks.note: Blender is documented in an official 5.3 manual for Linux, macOS, Windows and Steam. It is the free route to 3D avatars and animation, but the learning curve is steeper than a purpose-built avatar rigger. Use it if you want full control over the model and can invest the time.

sources.fact: The official Blender Manual is titled Blender 5.3 Manual and documents installation on Linux, macOS, Windows and Steam.
The Blender Manual has a section titled 'About Free Software and the GPL'.
The GitHub repository blender/blender is described as the official mirror of Blender.

picks.name: Reallusion
picks.pricing: No pricing shown on the homepage opened.
picks.note: Reallusion describes 3D character production and 2D cartoon animation across entertainment, metaverse and simulation uses, and its news section mentions a stylized 3D character creator for Unreal. It is a commercial suite, so it will not meet a strict free-tool requirement. Check the store for current prices before planning a budget.

sources.fact: Reallusion's homepage describes it as a platform for 3D character creation and animation across media entertainment, metaverse, digital twinning, ArchViz and AI simulation.
Reallusion's homepage headline describes it as 3D character production and 2D cartoon animation.
Reallusion's homepage includes a news item on how a game studio uses the Stylized 3D Character Creator for Unreal.

picks.name: Spine
picks.pricing: Free trial; Essential at $69 and Professional at $379 as one-time licenses with free updates.
picks.note: Spine is 2D skeletal animation software for video games, with runtimes for Unity, C#, cocos2d-x, iOS, Android, C++, HTML5 and JS. It is a poor choice for expressive faces compared with Live2D but a strong one for game sprites. The trial lets you check the workflow before you pay.

sources.fact: Esoteric Software describes Spine as 2D skeletal animation software for video games.
Esoteric Software's purchase page lists Spine Essential at $99 and $69, and Spine Professional at $449 and $379.
Esoteric Software's purchase page says all future updates are included without additional charges and that a Spine licence also permits use of the Spine Runtimes in games.

picks.name: Rive
picks.pricing: Free to build, with a splash screen on free exports; paid seats start at $9 per month.
picks.note: Rive pairs an editor with open-source runtimes for every platform, which helps when an avatar must live in an app or web page rather than a streaming program. Free exports show a splash screen that upgrades remove. It is less suited to VTuber face tracking, so verify your tracking app supports the format first.

sources.fact: Rive describes itself as an agent-native 2D and 3D engine for games, apps and UI.
Rive's pricing page lists Free, Cadet at $9 per seat per month, Voyager at $32 per seat per month and Enterprise at $120 per seat per month.
Rive's pricing page says building with Rive is free, but free exports play a Rive splash screen that is removed on upgrade.

picks.name: Moho
picks.best_for: Bone and mesh rigging for 2D animation
picks.pricing: One-time purchase: Moho Pro 14 at $399.99 and Moho Debut 14 at $59.99.
picks.note: Moho is 2D animation software with rigging, inverse kinematics, physics, distortion meshes and layered SVG and PSD support. Version 14.5 adds live playback to animate and stream characters in real time. It is a paid, one-time purchase, so it fits artists who want to own a rigging tool outright, though it is a general animation program and not a VTuber-specific one.

sources.fact: Moho's homepage describes it as animation software for 2D movies, films, commercials, cartoons, vector animation, stop motion and frame-by-frame animation.
The Moho buy page lists Moho Pro 14 as a one-time purchase at $399.99 and Moho Debut 14 at $59.99.
Moho's site footer states copyright 2026 LOSTMARBLE LLC.

picks.name: Animaze
picks.pricing: Free tier with 80+ free items; paid individual plans at $19.99 ($1.67/month) and $99.99 ($8.34/month).
picks.note: Animaze, by FaceRig, is software for livestreaming or video chat with custom 2D and 3D animated avatars, backgrounds and props. It skips the rigging step: you pick or import an avatar and go live. The pricing page lists Pro-Streamer commercial rights for streamers earning $6,000 per year, so check that line before monetizing a channel.

sources.fact: Animaze is software for livestreaming or video chat with custom 2D and 3D animated avatars, backgrounds and props.
Animaze's individual pricing page lists a free tier with access to 80+ free items including avatars, backgrounds, props and emotes.
Pro-Streamer commercial rights on the pricing page are for streamers earning $6,000 per year.

picks.name: Warudo
picks.pricing: Pricing is not shown in the text extracted from the homepage or pricing page.
picks.note: Warudo is 3D VTubing software with built-in face and hand tracking, custom 3D assets, Twitch and YouTube integration, a blueprint system and C# plugins. It pairs naturally with a move from a 2D puppet to a 3D model, and the handbook is available in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Spanish. Expect more setup than a plug-and-play avatar app.

sources.fact: Warudo is flexible 3D VTubing software with built-in face and hand tracking, custom 3D assets and Twitch and YouTube integration.
Warudo offers a blueprint system and C# plugins, according to its homepage.
The Warudo handbook is available in English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Spanish.

picks.name: VTube Studio
picks.best_for: Running Live2D models without the editor
picks.pricing: Available on Steam; the homepage shows no price in the extracted text.
picks.note: VTube Studio brings Live2D models to life with webcam tracking for Virtual YouTubers. It is not a rigging replacement, since it runs models made elsewhere, so treat it as the companion that lets you try a model from another editor before committing. Its site links to a Steam page, documentation and a license page.

sources.fact: VTube Studio is an app for Virtual YouTubers that makes it easy to bring your own Live2D models to life.
VTube Studio's homepage links to a Steam page for getting the app.
VTube Studio's official site has a license page and documentation.

how_to_pick: Decide whether your avatar stays 2D. If it does and you want open tools, Inochi2D is the first thing to download. If you are willing to switch to 3D, VRoid Studio gives the quickest start and Blender the deepest control. Game developers should weigh Spine or Rive against the engine they use. Before you commit, export a test model into your tracking app, because compatibility with VTube Studio or a similar program decides more than editor features. Moho suits artists who want a one-time-purchase rigger, Animaze skips rigging, Warudo covers 3D tracking, and VTube Studio is worth keeping as a test bench for any Live2D model.

faqs.q: Is there a fully free alternative to Live2D Cubism?
faqs.a: Inochi2D and Blender are the free-leaning options in this list. Inochi2D's homepage has Download and Donate links with no price, and Blender's manual covers the GPL. Live2D itself also keeps a FREE editor version after the 42-day PRO trial.

faqs.q: Can I use Inochi2D models for streaming?
faqs.a: The Inochi2D homepage says it is used for VTubing and games development. Check that your tracking software lists support for it, since not every app loads every format.

faqs.q: Does Live2D Cubism have a student discount?
faqs.a: The Live2D site mentions a Student Discount Program with a 76% OFF coupon for a 3-year Cubism Editor PRO subscription for eligible students. Confirm eligibility rules on Live2D's own page.

VRoid Studio, Reallusion and Blender work with 3D characters. VRoid Studio is listed as a 3D character creation tool, and Reallusion describes 3D character production. Blender is the general-purpose route. Warudo also targets 3D avatars with face and hand tracking.

faqs.q: Why is Ready Player Me not on this page?
faqs.a: We could not confirm its facts from pages opened for this review, so it is left out until it can be sourced.
